findings.passage: Focus Features is mounting a Best Actress Oscar campaign for her, according to Variety as relayed by [People](https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/movies/articles/inde-navarrette-thought-she-blew-184530143.html)
findings.problem: Misattribution. The linked Yahoo page (S55) is a Wealth of Geeks article by Marija Mrakovic syndicated on Yahoo: its schema.org provider is 'Wealth of Geeks' and it shows the Wealth of Geeks logo. It cites PEOPLE only for other items (the wigs, the May social-media interview). The campaign line itself ('according to Variety') is relayed accurately, but the article names the wrong outlet in reader-facing text, and the evidence record's S55 speaker ('Yahoo/People syndication') carries the same error.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence names the relay correctly (Wealth of Geeks, via Yahoo) or, better, links Variety's original report after opening it. S55's speaker/context are corrected in the evidence record, and the citation list matches. No other claim attributes S55 to People.

findings.passage: what keeps Six narrowly ahead is a handful of securing moves unrelated to her work.
findings.problem: Two of the named items are work-adjacent: 'in order to keep myself secure' answers a Variety question about decompressing from a character's emotions (S10 27:10-27:52), and the social-media limit was set because it was 'a new step in my career' (S49). What they share is that they are not about a verdict on her work, which is the distinction the Six case needs. The type FAQ repeats 'including in ways unrelated to her work'.
findings.acceptance_test: Body and Type 3 FAQ say the items are not about a verdict on her work (or similar) instead of 'unrelated to her work', with the items unchanged.

findings.passage: "I deleted all of them," she began on Variety's podcast, then corrected herself
findings.problem: S10 is Variety's 'Up Next' YouTube video interview ('welcome to Variety's Up Next'); nothing opened shows it is a podcast.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence calls it Variety's Up Next interview (or a Variety video interview), or a source shows it is distributed as a podcast.

(S40, and S41 audio ~44:50), 'created a really safe space' (S09 20:48-20:50) and Buchanan's 'this career that you're forging' (S42 0:05). findings.acceptance_test: Each quote's sentence is added to an existing claim's passage (C115, C48, C134) or given its own claim with source IDs and locators.

protected_checks.passage: Before _Obsession_ started shooting, Inde Navarrette told its writer-director, Curry Barker, two things.
She has described those years at least four ways:
The plan was his, and warming up a nervous lead is ordinary directing.
Against it, nearly all of this is self-report from a campaign that rewards candor about fear, and filtering social media is ordinary advice for anyone newly famous.
She has already named the test she wants. "I really want to prove that _Obsession_ wasn't just lightning in a bottle," she told Nylon in July 2026.
The first was a confession. "I said, 'I don't know how to scream, and I'm feeling very shy,'" she told [Collider's Perri Nemiroff](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEB4C4SIAbY) in May 2026.
- **Lonely**, to [Complex News](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IUAsUy_aKR8) in June 2026. Asked whether she kept friends, she said no: "making friends was always really difficult for me."
When the rapper Big Sean messaged her, her first thought, she told Complex News, was "Oh, no," and she handed the phone to her boyfriend to read it first. (It was kind.)
That one sentence holds both readings. Discomfort at not knowing what others think is a Six's. Fear of the verdict on her work is a Three's.
